chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mohsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fazl Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaaq, said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about two parents and two sisters (of the father and mother); would these two block the mother from the third? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So if they are three?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So if they are four?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.لِأَبٍ وَ أُمٍّ: of the father and mother (consanguineous and uterine)

ai.seo_question: How many siblings are required to block the mother from her one-third inheritance share?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific threshold in Shia jurisprudence where the presence of siblings reduces the mother's share from one-third to one-sixth, a ruling derived from the general principle in Surah An-Nisa. It highlights the scholarly consensus that while two siblings do not trigger this reduction (hijab), the accumulation of three or more siblings establishes the condition for diminishing her portion, reflecting the precise numerical logic applied in Usuli interpretation of inheritance laws.
